covered_actors: National data protection supervisory authorities (SAs) in the EEA
Data controllers developing or deploying AI models trained with personal data
enforcement_authorities: National data protection supervisory authorities (SAs) in the EEA
penalties_summary: Under Article 58 GDPR, national supervisory authorities enjoy discretionary powers to impose appropriate, necessary, and proportionate corrective measures upon finding an infringement, including issuing administrative fines, imposing temporary limitations on processing, ordering ex officio erasure of unlawfully processed personal data or part of the training dataset, or—where necessary and proportionate—ordering the erasure of the entire training dataset and/or the AI model itself, without prejudice to enforcement under the EU AI Act or civil liability frameworks.
implementation_notes: Adopted pursuant to Article 64(2) GDPR following a 4 September 2024 request from the Irish supervisory authority, this Opinion is addressed to all EEA supervisory authorities to promote consistent GDPR application across the EEA. It provides a non-exhaustive, case-by-case analytical framework on AI model anonymity, legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR) in development and deployment, and the downstream consequences of unlawful training data processing, without prejudice to controllers' and processors' existing GDPR obligations. It explicitly excludes detailed analysis of special categories of data (Article 9), automated decision-making (Article 22), purpose compatibility (Article 6(4)), DPIAs (Article 35), and data protection by design (Article 25), and notes forthcoming EDPB guidelines on anonymisation, pseudonymisation, and data scraping for generative AI.
